summary: Announces a mail server at UCSB listening on socket 3 that implements the small part of FTP needed to deliver mail: the MAIL and BYE commands. It lists the UCSB users who could receive network mail and their user names.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 574 announces that UCSB could receive network mail through a server on socket 3. It names the supported commands and lists the people and general address that could receive mail.

subtitle: An announcement of UCSB's network mail service.

tldr.problem: People on the network needed a way to send mail to users at UCSB.
tldr.mechanism: A UCSB server on socket 3 implemented the MAIL and BYE commands, the subset of FTP the announcement says was needed for mail delivery.
tldr.outcome: The announcement lists six individual recipient names and the general address GRIPE.

today: RFC 574 is a historical announcement of a mail facility at UCSB.

sections.title: The UCSB Mail Facility
sections.content: UCSB announced a server program resident under socket 3. It supported the subset of the File Transfer Protocol needed for mail delivery, with only the MAIL and BYE commands implemented at the time of the announcement.
sections.plainLanguage: A UCSB server accepted network mail through a limited set of FTP commands. At the time, it supported MAIL for mail delivery and BYE to end the exchange.

sections.title: Mail Recipients
sections.content: A sender addressed mail to an individual by giving that person's local UCSB user name in the MAIL command. The announcement names FAEH, GUYTON, KRILANOV, MOSSO, PICKENS and STOUGHTN as valid recipients. It also lists GRIPE for general comments or complaints about UCSB services.
sections.plainLanguage: Senders used a local user name to address one of the listed UCSB recipients. They could send general comments or complaints to GRIPE.

sections.title: Scope of the Announcement
sections.content: This RFC announces the existence and limited command set of the UCSB mail server. It does not describe a general mail protocol or provide details beyond the supported commands and recipient names.
sections.plainLanguage: The note announces one site's mail service and who could receive messages there. It does not define a general network mail system.
